subject: Sparkline SDK support and deprecation playbook
messages:
From: John Doe <john@sparkline.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Integrations <integrations@sparkline.ai>
Date: Sat, 29 May 2027 16:15:00 -0700
Subject: Question: SDK deprecation window and migration options for Sparkline integration

Hi Marcus,

Quick one from our side — we're preparing a major release of Sparkline (v3.0) and our engineering org plans to stop shipping the legacy Redwood SDK shim we've been running in production. We saw the announcement about the SDK deprecation roadmap on the partner portal, but need concrete timelines and supported migration options for the Sparkline connector.

Context: our integration uses the legacy batching / connection pool behavior (v1.x) and also relies on the SDK's built-in KV cache management for prompt prefixes. We need to understand:
- Exact sunset date for v1.x shims and grace period for functional parity
- Recommended migration path (native API vs new SDK bridge) and any code examples
- Whether Redwood can provide a short-lived compatibility bridge or backport patch for batching semantics

Can we get a playbook we can share with our product and infra teams this week? We're under a customer SLA and need to include the migration window in our release notes.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick 30-min call if that helps.

John
Head of Integrations, Sparkline AI

PS — attaching a one-page overview of our integration hotspots (sparkline-migration-outline.pdf).

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: John Doe <john@sparkline.ai>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 30 May 2027 08:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Question: SDK deprecation window and migration options for Sparkline integration

John — thanks for the clear ask and for the attachment. We appreciate the heads-up on Sparkline v3.0.

High-level response and proposal: we can offer a two-track approach: a) a 6-month compatibility bridge (managed by Redwood) that preserves v1.x batching and prefix-caching semantics, and b) an official migration guide for moving to the new native API pattern and the v2.x SDK (recommended long-term).

Proposal details (summary):
- Sunset & grace period: we propose a formal deprecation announcement now, with an official sunset date of 2027-12-31 for the legacy shim, and a mandatory cutover by 2028-03-31. This gives a minimum 9-month runway from now.
- Managed compatibility bridge: 6 months (2027-06-01 to 2027-11-30) as an optional add-on for partners who need immediate parity. Bridge includes batching behavior, KV cache emulation, and request routing rules.
- Migration artifacts: a migration guide, code snippets, and a test suite to validate request/response parity; we'll provide a reference implementation and a small backport patch if necessary.
- Rollout support: one joint weekly office hour for the first 8 weeks, plus a single on-site/virtual migration debug session for Sparkline engineering.

Next steps I propose:
1) Vanessa (cc'd) will scope the bridge effort and provide an estimated SOW and cost.
2) Laura (cc'd, product) will draft the migration guide and test-suite checklist.
3) Marcus will schedule a 30-min kickoff this week to align on integration hotspots.

We can attach the detailed bridge proposal doc and SOW once Vanessa completes scoping.

If this sounds OK, can you confirm Sparkline's preferred runway (6 vs 9 months for paid bridge) and any blackout dates for your release schedule?

—Marcus
Head of Partner Engineering, Redwood Inference

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: John Doe <john@sparkline.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 30 May 2027 09:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Question: SDK deprecation window and migration options for Sparkline integration

Hi John — thanks, this is actionable. I'm attaching the initial bridge scoping doc (redwood-sdk-bridge-proposal.md) as an internal draft; it outlines engineering effort, compatibility coverage matrix, and a provisional cost model. High-level notes:

- Estimated engineering: 4 engineer-weeks to implement emulation for batching + KV prefix behavior; additional 1 week for QA and the parity test harness.
- Compatibility coverage: request routing, prefix caching, streaming behavior; notable gap: low-level connection pooling semantics that depend on Sparkline's run-time (we'll need a small runtime adapter).
- Cost model: fixed-fee bridge + optional hourly support for debugging post-cutover.

We should confirm whether Sparkline prefers that we host the bridge (Redwood-managed) or deliver artifacts for Sparkline to run in their infra. Hosting reduces their operational lift but adds to Redwood's support commitments.

Marcus — I'm available Tue-Thu next week for the kickoff. John — can you confirm which model you prefer?

Thanks — Vanessa
Director, Alliances, Redwood Inference

Date: Sun, 30 May 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Question: SDK deprecation window and migration options for Sparkline integration

Thanks Marcus and Vanessa — the proposal looks reasonable and gives us breathing room. A few quick clarifications:

1) Sparkline prefers Redwood-hosted bridge for the initial 6 months; operationally that's the easiest path for us.
2) We'd like the migration guide and parity test suite no later than 2027-07-15 so we can begin internal validation.
3) Blackout windows: our feature freeze for v3.0 begins 2027-08-01; we need the first compatibility tests before that date.

If you can send the SOW and an initial contract addendum for the bridge by EOD Tuesday (2027-06-01), we can get procurement moving. I'll also share the internal runbook and a small sampling of production telemetry for one customer to help narrow the compatibility gaps.

Appreciate the quick turnaround. Looking forward to the kickoff — please send an invite for Tue morning Pacific.

John
Head of Integrations, Sparkline AI
